_meta.purpose: Seed catalog for the 'search your catalog' intake path in the mini-site builder guide. Load this array, let users search by name/category, and hand the matched entry straight to classify()/the three-lane fetch model.

schema.source_kind: matches the classify() adapter types: arcgis | socrata | ckan | json | geojson | feed
schema.auth_tier: matches the three-lane fetch model: none | instant_key | oauth
schema.shape: matches the normalize() output shape: single | table | geo | series | feed

_meta.caution: Auth tiers and rate limits drift. Three entries below already changed within the last two months of research for this file (rest-countries, balldontlie, courtlistener) — spot-check anything here against its live docs before shipping, don't treat this file as permanently accurate.

sources.name: NASA Open APIs (APOD, NeoWs, DONKI, Mars Rover Photos)
sources.notes: DEMO_KEY works immediately at 30 req/hr and 50/day per IP; a free key removes that ceiling.

sources.name: USGS Earthquake Feed
sources.notes: Real-time GeoJSON. Swap 'all_day' for other rolling windows and magnitude cuts at the same path.

sources.name: National Weather Service (api.weather.gov)
sources.notes: No key — send an identifying User-Agent header instead. US coverage only.

sources.name: Open-Meteo
sources.notes: Built specifically so weather data never needs a signup; free for non-commercial use.

sources.name: GBIF Species Occurrences
sources.notes: Hundreds of millions of biodiversity occurrence records, free and open.

sources.name: iNaturalist Observations
sources.notes: Citizen-science species observations; read endpoints are open.

sources.name: Open Food Facts
sources.notes: Crowdsourced barcode/nutrition database. Explicitly no key, no hard limit.

sources.name: Wikidata SPARQL Endpoint
sources.notes: A queryable graph of almost everything. Steepest learning curve on this list (SPARQL), highest ceiling.

sources.name: Wikipedia / Wikimedia REST API
sources.notes: Summaries, page media, search — no key.

sources.name: Open Library
sources.notes: Book metadata and cover art, an Internet Archive project.

sources.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access
sources.notes: 470,000+ artworks, public-domain images included where rights allow.

sources.name: Internet Archive Advanced Search
sources.notes: Also worth calling on every scheduled fetch elsewhere in the app for provenance snapshots, not just as its own source.

sources.name: SEC EDGAR Full-Text & Filings
sources.notes: No key, but the SEC requires a descriptive User-Agent identifying you and your contact info, or you'll get blocked.

sources.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data)
sources.notes: Every major US economic time series. Instant free key, generous limits.

sources.name: World Bank Indicators API
sources.notes: Global development and economic indicators, no key.

sources.name: USAspending.gov
sources.notes: Federal contracts, grants, and loans. No key, POST-based search.

sources.name: OpenCorporates
sources.notes: The shell-company layer. Free tier is rate-limited and excludes some jurisdictions and fields.

sources.name: CourtListener / RECAP
sources.notes: Free-account default dropped sharply on 2026-05-07 to roughly 5 req/min, 50/hr, 125/day (rolling window). Ignore older tutorials citing a 5,000/hr default — that's gone. Academic/EDU accounts get more.

sources.name: OpenFEC (Federal Election Commission)
sources.notes: DEMO_KEY works immediately for light testing; register for anything sustained.

sources.name: Congress.gov API
sources.notes: Bills, members, votes. Instant free key.

sources.name: US Census Bureau API
sources.notes: Light testing often works keyless; a free key is expected for anything sustained.

sources.name: GDELT DOC 2.0 API
sources.notes: Global news coded into structured events from worldwide coverage. Free, no key, rolling ~3-month full-text window.

sources.name: Generic ArcGIS REST Feature/MapServer layer
sources.notes: A pattern, not one dataset — nearly every US city/county GIS office runs this stack (e.g. maps.nashville.gov). Hit the root with ?f=json first to enumerate what a given host offers.

sources.name: Generic Socrata city/state portal
sources.notes: Pattern — e.g. data.nashville.gov, data.cityofchicago.org. The Discovery API can enumerate a whole portal's datasets before you pick one.

sources.name: data.gov (CKAN Action API)
sources.notes: Federal plus a large share of state/local open-data catalogs run CKAN underneath this same action API.

sources.name: Zippopotam.us
sources.notes: Postal code to place lookup. Dead simple, no key.

sources.name: OSM Nominatim Geocoding
sources.notes: No key, but requires an identifying User-Agent and is capped around 1 req/sec. Fine for a mini-site, not for bulk geocoding.

sources.name: REST Countries
sources.notes: Changed recently: the old keyless v3.1 is deprecated and returns errors. v5 requires a free key (500 req/mo, no card). Update any bookmarked v3.1 snippets.

sources.name: Free Dictionary API
sources.notes: Definitions, phonetics, audio links. No key.

sources.name: Datamuse
sources.notes: Word-relationship queries: rhymes, means-like, sounds-like. No key.

sources.name: Open Trivia Database
sources.notes: Good stand-in dataset for testing the table-shape template end to end.

sources.name: Deck of Cards API
sources.notes: Stateful-feeling but stateless underneath. Useful minimal test case for the 'single' shape.

sources.name: JSONPlaceholder
sources.notes: Fake but stable REST data. Good for testing the ingestion pipeline before pointing it at anything real.

sources.name: Advice Slip API
sources.notes: Tiny single-value payload. Good minimal test case for the 'single' shape template.
